title: Piedmont Crescent Bank Deposit Rate Sheet: Certificate of Deposit Terms and Published Rates
content:
Rates published for Certificates of Deposit take effect on the date of this sheet and are fixed onto a certificate at the start of each term.

## 1. Published schedule

| Tier | Term, months | Rate structure | Standard interest rate, percent | Standard annual percentage yield, percent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 6 | fixed | 3.78 | 3.85 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 11 | fixed, with no penalty after the opening days | 3.54 | 3.60 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 12 | fixed | 3.97 | 4.05 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 18 | bump-up, allowing one rate increase | 3.83 | 3.90 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 36 | fixed | 3.49 | 3.55 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 60 | fixed | 3.39 | 3.45 |

The standard interest rate is the published rate for a new term of the tier before any bonus points. The standard annual percentage yield is the published yield for a new term of the tier before any bonus points, and it is the yield the standard interest rate produces when compounded daily.

## 2. Compounding and day count

On every tier of the Certificates of Deposit line, accrued interest is added to the interest base daily, and the year used to work out a day of interest is 365 days.

| Tier | Compounding | Days in the year |
|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | daily | 365 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | daily | 365 |
| 12-Month Certificate | daily | 365 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | daily | 365 |
| 36-Month Certificate | daily | 365 |
| 60-Month Certificate | daily | 365 |

## 3. Notes on reading the sheet

The two columns of rates are not alternatives. The interest rate is the figure interest is worked out at; the annual percentage yield is the figure quoted to the customer as the yearly return. Every tier of the Certificates of Deposit line publishes both, and the pair moves together.

The longest terms on this sheet do not carry the highest rates. The 12-Month Certificate pays the highest standard yield at 4.05 percent, while the 60-Month Certificate pays 3.45 percent, and the 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate pays 3.60 percent in exchange for its penalty structure.
